newsitem.title: USA: P&G says lower costs helped Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: P&G says lower costs helped Q2 earnings.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co said Tuesday its second quarter earnings of $1.35 a primary share versus $1.18 were helped by favorable commodity prices and continued cost reduction efforts.

"Our net earnings for the quarter were strong, reflecting favorable commodity prices and our continued efforts to reduce costs through simplication and standardization across the company," chairman and chief executive John Pepper said in a statement.
"Although improved from last quarter, our priority remains to accelerate sales and unit volume growth," he said.

The consumer products giant expects that growth to come through new product initiatives, production capacity P&G is adding and continuing roll-out of P&G's Efficient Consumer Response, an inventory, shelf space management and promotions program with retailers.
Worldwide unit volume was a record, growing two percent from the year-ago quarter, P&G said.
Sales grew one percent to $9.14 billion, P&G said, adding the difference between sales and unit volume growth was largely due to weaker currencies in Europe and Asia.
For the six months, worldwide volume was up two percent over the year-ago six months while sales were stable, primarily reflecting unfavorable exchange rates.
Cost reduction efforts and lower commodity prices, especially pulp, also helped six-month earnings, P&G said.
Pepper said cost reduction efforts were also helping cash flow for the six months, enabling a share repurchase program and reduction of debt.
